trigger: a commit to deploy/packaging/windows/yuzu-agent.iss using an ISPP short directive (#+ include, #= emit, #: define, #? if, ...) or a {#...} expansion outside [Files] (e.g. AppName=X{#NewLine}[Files]{#NewLine}Source: ...; Flags: recursesubdirs), or any {#expr} in a quoted Source directory

Parser/gate half verified by security-guardian and end to end by chaos-injector (generate exit 0, check OK, no incomplete reason, and the contents note/::warning:: falsely say the ISPP-installed file is 'not installed'); ISCC half read from issrc source and CONFIRMED by cross-platform (no ISCC run). No such form in today's .iss. Reporter listed no EXPOSURE class; the recorder maps a committer within their own privilege to E3, which changes nothing. E6 not established (a future .iss edit is the parser's production input); E7 not applicable (the check gates the release). Convergence: variant-of g8-sec-1 (third pass of this class). Suggested remedy (security-guardian): freeze a rule instead of emulating ISPP further: refuse every line whose first non-blank char is '#' except the known header block, and refuse '{#' everywhere except an exact {#Name} of a header default.
summary: The .iss parser misses ISPP short directives and {#...} expansions outside [Files]; an installer SBOM can silently under-list and state injected files are not installed.

Reporter's native MEDIUM disagrees with its own facts: I3 derives HIGH; recorded at the derived band as the reporter itself stated. E7 not applicable (release asset). Convergence: variant-of p4-sg-1.
summary: '[ Files ]' is mapped by the parser but ignored by ISCC; the installer SBOM over-lists with no warning.
